findings.title: Default upgrade-strategy test never enables rolling-updates feature
findings.body: In createInitialDeployment the method returns early when updateStrategy is null without configuring spec.features.enabled to include rolling-updates, while the RECREATE path does configure it. The guide added in the same PR states the Operator requires the rolling-updates preview feature or it will fail. As a result the parameterized cases with null/default strategy run without the required feature, so they fail for the wrong reason and never exercise the intended default-strategy upgrade path. The feature setup must happen before the early return for all strategies.

findings.title: Failure exit codes for update-compatibility tool are not verified
findings.body: The documented contract for automation is the exit code: 0 rolling possible, 3 recreate required, 4 feature rolling-updates disabled. This PR renumbers RECREATE from 4 to 3 and adds 4 for disabled, but testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the stderr text and never asserts exit code 4, and testWrongVersions never asserts exit code 3. Only the happy path asserts exit code 0. A regression that prints the correct message but returns the wrong code, including 0 on failure, would pass tests and break scripts and operator logic that branches on the exit code.

findings.title: Docs claim Operator fails without rolling-updates, breaking all existing CRs
findings.body: The added CAUTION says while in preview the rolling-updates feature must be enabled otherwise the Keycloak Operator will fail. Rolling-updates is a new feature so every existing Keycloak CR lacks it. Failing all reconciliations until every CR is edited is an unnecessary breaking change. The compatible behavior is to fall back to pre-existing behavior when the feature is disabled and only fail the specific CR that requests the preview update strategy without the flag. As written the docs either mandate an overly broad outage or are inaccurate since no operator code in the PR scopes the failure.
